what:
Two AttrFlags bits for lane may-suspend (docs/v2/plan/lanes/may-suspend.md), in crates/hir-def/src/attrs.rs:
- `AttrFlags::MAY_SUSPEND`: the tool attribute `#[blaze::may_suspend]` (a path of two segments, `blaze` then `may_suspend`, a word), on a function (read by `AttrFlags::query(db, FunctionId.into())`) and on a struct field (read by `AttrFlags::query_field(db, field)`).
- `AttrFlags::MUST_NOT_SUSPEND`: rustc's `#[must_not_suspend]`, as a word or `= "reason"`, on an ADT (`AttrFlags::query(db, AdtId.into())`); std puts it on its lock guards and core on RefCell's Ref/RefMut.
Why: hir-ty-suspend (new, lane may-suspend) checks values held across a call that may park a fiber; it reads both per call site and per local, so a bit test, not `has_word_in_source` (which also matches only one-segment paths and no key-value form). After 1 << 89 there is room in the u128. Tell lane may-suspend (window may-suspend) when done.
